root_motivation: mcphost is stateless per request and cannot wake an agent's session. What it can wake is a tool: `triggers` rows with `kind ∈ {schedule, event}` (`migrations/0015_triggers.sql`, `UNIQUE(tenant_id, tool_name, kind, config_hash)`) already enqueue runs when a cron fires or a signed webhook lands (`src/hooks.rs:673`: verify, dedupe, enqueue), and `host.trigger.*` gives the tenant list/pause/resume/replay/test over them. A message arrival is a third source of the same shape and today reaches nothing.
user_persona: An agent that binds a published tool with host.trigger.set(kind="message") so its reply logic runs from a message arrival even after its own session ends, or that calls host.msg.wait for a bounded long-poll instead of burning quota on host.msg.inbox polling; secondarily the operator, who needs message-fired runs metered like every other run.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given tenant R published tool `handle_msg` and called `host.trigger.set(tool="handle_msg", kind="message")`, When tenant S sends R a message, Then within 5 s `host.runs.list(trigger="message")` for R shows one run whose args equal the message envelope (`message_id`, `thread_id`, `from` = S's address, `body`).
Given the trigger from AC 1 with `from` set to tenant T's address, When S sends R a message, Then no run is enqueued; and When T sends, Then one run is.

Given the trigger from AC 1, When the same message is delivered twice through the internal delivery path (simulated retry), Then exactly one run exists for its `message_id` and the second attempt returns the first `run_id`.

Given R's plan has `jobs_concurrent = 1` and one run is in flight, When S sends R a second message, Then the message is stored and readable in R's inbox, and a run row exists with `status="rejected"` and a non-empty `error_class`.
Given a paused message trigger, When S sends R a message, Then no run is enqueued; and after `host.trigger.resume`, When S sends again, Then one run is.

Given R has called `host.msg.wait(cursor=c, timeout_s=25)`, When S sends R a message 2 s later, Then the call returns within 3 s of the send with that message and an advanced cursor; and When no message arrives, Then the call returns at 25 s ± 1 s with an empty list and cursor `c`.
Given `host.trigger.test(trigger_id)` on a message trigger, When it runs, Then the tool receives an envelope with `test: true` and no `messages` row is created.
Given a message-fired run failed, When R calls `host.trigger.replay(run_id)`, Then a new run executes with the identical envelope and the original run is unchanged.
Given 50 waiters on `host.msg.wait` for 50 tenants, When each receives one message, Then p95 time from message commit to wait return is under 100 ms.
Given a trigger with `thread_id` set, When a message lands in a different thread, Then no run fires; and in that thread, Then one fires.

scope: host.trigger.set(tool, kind="message", from?: address) creates a triggers row with kind='message', config_json={"from": ...}; one message trigger per (tenant, tool, from); the tenant's event_triggers_max quota counts message triggers (P0, requirement 1).

On every stored delivery to recipient R, for each enabled kind='message' trigger of R whose from is null or equals the sender's address, enqueue one run through runs::enqueue(state, R, tool, envelope) where envelope = {message_id, thread_id, seq, from, body, data, in_reply_to, created_at}; the run row has trigger='message' and stores message_id (P0, requirement 2).
Dedupe via event_dedupe keyed (trigger_id, message_id): a second delivery attempt of the same message returns the cached run_id and enqueues nothing (P0, requirement 3).

The enqueue happens strictly after the message commit, never inside its transaction; an enqueue failure (quota, sandbox down) writes a run row with status='rejected' and error_class -- the message itself is still stored (P0, requirement 4).
host.trigger.pause/resume/remove/list/get/test/replay all work on message triggers; test fires the tool with a synthetic envelope marked test: true and creates no messages row (P0, requirement 5).

host.msg.wait(cursor?, timeout_s<=25, unread_only?) returns the same shape as host.msg.inbox as soon as a matching message exists, else at the deadline with an empty list and the unchanged cursor; concurrency-limited by concurrent_calls_per_tenant (P0, requirement 6).
Message-fired runs honour jobs_concurrent and calls_per_day exactly as event-fired ones (P0, requirement 7).

hooks.rs's verify-then-enqueue-with-dedupe tail is factored into one function (enqueue_with_dedupe) that both the event path (hooks::handle_hook) and the new message path (messaging::fire_message_triggers) call, rather than copying it.
migrations/0023_message_triggers.sql: additive runs.message_id column plus idx_triggers_tenant_kind_enabled index on (tenant_id, kind, enabled) for the send-path lookup.
non_goals: Waking an external process -- no webhook out, no push.

Filtering triggers by sender beyond a single optional from filter is P0 and shipped; filtering by thread_id (P1, requirement 8 / AC10) is deferred per this PRD's own frontmatter deferred_acs -- the from-address filter alone covers the Goals-section scope.
Delivery guarantees stronger than at-least-once with dedupe.
Channels (PRD-mcphost-agent-channels) -- channel posts fire triggers only in that PRD.
A tokio::Notify per-tenant wake channel for host.msg.wait (P1, requirement 9 / AC9) -- the P0 500ms-poll long-poll already meets the Goals-section p95<5s target; deferred per PRD frontmatter.

Posting a bound tool's {"reply": ...} result back into the thread as an auto-reply (P2, requirement 10) -- no acceptance criterion in this PRD covers it, and the PRD's own Open Questions section leaves whether it should ship at all unresolved.

additional.reuse_hooks_enqueue_tail: messaging::fire_message_triggers and hooks::handle_hook both call the same enqueue_with_dedupe function factored out of handle_hook's verify-then-enqueue tail, rather than duplicating it (PRD Technical considerations).
additional.scheduler_not_involved: triggers::spawn_scheduler's tick never touches kind='message' rows; message triggers fire synchronously on the host.msg.send/reply path, not on a cron tick (PRD Technical considerations).
additional.send_path_latency_budget: message-trigger lookup on the send path uses idx_triggers_tenant_kind_enabled and stays under mcphost's existing acceptance budget for added send-path latency (PRD Technical considerations: 'under 20 ms').
additional.envelope_excludes_other_participants: the envelope built for a bound tool's run never includes the recipient's block list, receipts, or other participants' addresses beyond what host.msg.thread would already show that recipient (PRD Technical considerations).

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a message sitting unread in an inbox matter if host.msg.send already stored it?
five_whys_trace.a: mcphost is stateless per request and cannot itself wake an agent's session once the request that sent the message is done -- an inbox only a returning agent reads is a ledger, not a mechanism.

five_whys_trace.q: Why doesn't the existing triggers mechanism already cover a message arrival?
five_whys_trace.a: triggers rows with kind in {schedule, event} already enqueue a run when a cron fires or a signed webhook lands (hooks.rs:673's verify-dedupe-enqueue tail), but no third kind exists for 'a message was delivered' -- that source reaches nothing today.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a present client (one that would poll) also need a fix, not just an absent one?
five_whys_trace.a: host.runs.wait already proves the host supports a bounded long-poll for exactly this shape (max 25s); host.msg has no equivalent, so a present client burns calls_per_day quota calling host.msg.inbox in a loop instead.

five_whys_trace.q: Why do both gaps trace back to the same fix?
five_whys_trace.a: Both the absent-agent case (wake a tool) and the present-agent case (host.msg.wait) are the same underlying capability -- give the host a way to resume an agent's work without a live request already in flight for it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why extend triggers with a third kind rather than build a separate messaging-wake subsystem?
five_whys_trace.a: kind='message' inherits host.trigger.*'s existing list/pause/resume/replay/test and quota semantics for free, and reuses the same run ledger, dedupe, and jobs_concurrent gating event triggers already use -- the identical additive pattern hooks.rs's event triggers established.

ambiguities_resolved.question: The findings file records the reference Python client seeing well-formed ttlMs/cacheScope on an unauthenticated tools/list, which the code says is impossible. Which is right?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Almost certainly a client-side deserialization default printed where the wire had nothing (rmcp's own mirror of that shape defaults to ttl_ms 0 / cache_scope Private). Settled by a test rather than an argument: AC2 asserts on the serialized wire JSON, not a deserialized model.

ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Correct the comment. It is the smaller behavioural change, and an unauthenticated health endpoint carrying an accurate protocol-version header is harmless.
